title: What Is Monitored Containment? — Council of AI Answer-First Guide (2026-09-29)
context: 2026-09-29 EAT cycle — Council of AI measurement board (14 axes, 19+ models, Ed25519-signed manifests). Monitored containment is not a marketing claim of 'uncrackable safety'; it is a continuous measurement claim about auditability. The verified measurement credential distinguishes true negatives from parse noise (e.g., det 0.000 = parse failure, not safety passage).
body: Monitored containment starts from an honest engineering premise: no static sandbox and no formal verification of a frontier LLM can deliver provable isolation against a sufficiently capable model. Side channels, distribution drift, and measurement-harness exploitation are always possible. The Council of AI responds not with a false isolation promise but with continuous, signed measurement across 14 axes (detector interoperability, care, privacy, reliability, and 10 others). Each axis carries a bank of canonical items (33–200), a spread of 19+ model scores, and an Ed25519-signed manifest that freezes board state. The verified measurement credential ties observation to the measuring party: a det score of 0.879 for deepseek-r1:8b means something different from 0.000 — the latter is parse noise, not safety passage. The containment index (append-only, signed) records incidents — jailbreak chains, refusal-policy degradations, self-exfiltration probes — giving regulators, deployers, and insurers a readable evidence stream for EU AI Act Art 9 (risk management) and Art 50(2) (machine-readable marking) without relying on unverifiable certification.
